title: Structs with Functions
story: Your contact app is growing fast. Instead of manually typing `Person{ name: "...", age: ... }` every time, you want a function that builds a Person for you — like a factory!
why: Functions that take structs as parameters and return structs let you create and transform data with reusable, clean logic.
analogy: A factory function is like a 3D printer — you give it raw materials (parameters) and it prints a finished object (struct instance).
try_it: Write a `create_family` function that takes four names and ages, returns a Person for each, and prints the name of the oldest family member.
tips: A function's return type can be any type — including a struct you defined
Use factory functions to centralize struct creation — if the struct changes, update one place
Name factory functions with `create_` or `make_` prefixes to signal they produce new instances
common_mistakes: Trying to access struct fields on a non-struct parameter — check that the parameter type is actually the struct
Forgetting to specify the return type as `-> Person` — the compiler needs to know what you're returning
Creating a struct inside the function but forgetting to `return` it
